chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever is in a place where he cannot reach the ground, let him bow with a gesture."

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ: Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.إِيمَاءً: a gesture or nod indicating the action of bowing

ai.seo_question: How should one perform the bowing (ruku') in prayer if they cannot reach the ground?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the concession (*rukhsa*) for the bowing (*ruku'*) in prayer when physical prostration on the ground is impossible, such as for the drowning (*al-ghariq*) or the stranded (*al-mutawahlil*). It establishes that a gesture of the head or body suffices as a valid substitute for the physical act, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease in times of necessity. This ruling is foundational for understanding the flexibility of ritual purity and prayer postures in extreme conditions.
